- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in the late part of the forecast horizon, particularly when the true values show a downward trend.
- Model tends to overreact to recent high values, causing overshoots followed by sharp corrections.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted — model fails to anticipate gradual pullback after peaks.
- Forecast lags behind true values in the first 5–10 days, then gradually catches up.
- Avoid extrapolating recent volatility into future periods; reduce sensitivity to short-term noise.
- When true values show a clear downward trend, model should reduce forecast slope more aggressively.
- Don’t assume momentum continues — especially after a sharp spike, prices often revert to prior mean.
